full_judgment:
3. Plaintiffs case, in short, is that 20.07 acres of land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 6 Ext. C originally belonged to one Jaki Palan who died leaving 2 sons named Alim Palan and Kalim, Palan and a widow Alimerma who subsequently died leaving her aforesaid two sons. Thereafter Alim Palan died leaving a son Hamid Palan by his first wife and another son Khalil and daughter Kaliarma by his second wife and a widow Kalimonnessa. Then died Hamid Palan leaving a son Moslehuddin, daughter Sarban and a widow who died leaving the aforesaid son and daughter as her heirs. Then died Sarban leaving husband Azam Ali and a son Ashraf Ali, daughter Rani Bibi as her heirs who sold their shares in the said property to defendant No. 1 Nurul Islam son of aforesaid Moslehuddin. Then died Moslehuddin leaving son defendant No. 1 Nurul Islam and daughter defendant No. 2 Banesa Bibi and a widow Golesa Bibi who subsequently Nika married plaintiff No. 1 Harez Ali Palan. Thereafter she died leaving her husband plaintiff No. 1 and her son and daughter defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by her first husband and 3 daughter’s plaintiff No. 6 Feroza Khatoon, Ajarennessa and Aulia Begum as her daughters by her second husband plaintiff No. 1 Harez Ali. Subsequently Ajarennessa and Aulia Begum died childless. Then died Khalil leaving mother Kalimonnessa, sister Kaliarma, uterine brothers Ahsan, and plaintiff No. 3 Jamu and uterine sister Ayatunnessa and uncle Kalim as his heirs. Then died Kalimonnessa leaving her second husband Kalim, sons Ahsan and plaintiff No. 8, Jamu and daughter Ayatunnessa as her heirs. Then died Ahsan leaving 2 sons plaintiff No. 1 Harez Ali and plaintiff No. 2 Afsaruddin and a daughter Maleka and widow plaintiff No. 4, Rabia Khatoon and father Kalim. Thereafter Maleka died leaving husband plaintiff No. 5 Habizuddin and brothers Harez Ali and Afsaruddin and mother Rabia Khatoon. Then died Kalim Palan leaving his son plaintiff No. 3 Jamu Palan and a daughter Ayatunncssa by his second wife Kalimannessa and sons Nazim Palan and Mazam Palan by his predeceased first wife. Thereafter Ayatunnessa died leaving her husband Moniruddin and brother Jamu. Then died Moniruddin leaving defendant Nos. 20 to 35 as his widow, sons and daughters. Then died Nazim Palan leaving defendant No. 3 Mokbulur Nessa as widow, defendant No. 4 Ishaque Palan and defendant No. 5 Gafur Palan as two sons, defendant No. 6 Sonaban and defendant No. 7 Tukunninessa and Moklesunnessa as 3 daughters. Then died Moklcsunnessa leaving defendant No. 8 Shcru, defendant No. 9 Surju and defendant No. 10 Hachunia as 3 sons, defendant No. 11 Momuza, defendant No. 13 Fazila Khatoon as two daughters and defendant No. 12 Majid as her husband. Then died Mozam Palan leaving defendant No. 14 Jamila Khatoon as widow, daughter Alecha and consanguine brother plaintiff No. 3 Zamu. Then died Alecha leaving defendant No. 14 Jamila Khatoon as mother and defendant No. 15 Siddique Darjee as husband, defendant No. 16 Ahsan and defendant No. 17 Ahmed as sons and defendant No. 18 Anwari Bibi and defendant No. 19 Regia Khatoon, as her daughters. 

 8. At the original trial the plaintiffs examined plaintiff No. 1, Harez Ali as PW 1 and plaintiff No. 3 Zamu Palan as PW 2 in support of their case and also filed and proved the two deeds of gift Exts. 1 and 1(a). After remand PW 1 was further examined on recall. The defendants examined defendant No. 1 as DW 1 and defendant 15 as DW 2. In support of prayer of the defendant Nos. 14(Ka) and 14(Kha) for Saham defendant No. 14(Kha) deposed as DW 3. Contesting defendants also produced and proved the sale deed dated 16.3.53 executed by Ashraf Ali and another in favour of defendant No. 1, Ext. A and certified copy of deed of gift dated 25.3.46 Ext. B executed by Mazam Ali in favour of Alecha Khatoon and certified copy of CS Khatian No. 6 Ext. C.
